items.prose: Derive the derivative of $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ from rules you have.
items.question: Put the lines of the derivation in order.

lines.text: $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$: a quotient with $u = \sin x$ and $v = \cos x$
$u' = \cos x$ and $v' = -\sin x$: the standard derivatives
$(\tan x)' = \dfrac{\cos x \cdot \cos x - \sin x \cdot (-\sin x)}{\cos^2 x}$: the quotient rule, $u'v - uv'$ over $v^2$
$= \dfrac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}$: two minus signs make a plus

items.question: Find $D$ at $y = 0.04$, to three decimal places.

explain.text: $P'(y) = -500(1 + y)^{-6}$, so $-\dfrac{P'}{P} = \dfrac{500(1 + y)^{-6}}{100(1 + y)^{-5}} = \dfrac{5}{1 + y}$. At 4% that is 4.808. A 0.01 rise in yield cuts the price by about 4.8%.

items.title: A bond price along a yield path
items.prompt:
A 5-year zero-coupon bond pays £100. With a continuous yield $y$ its price is $P(y) = 100e^{-5y}$. Today $y = 0.04$, and the yield is rising by 0.002 a month, so $y(t) = 0.04 + 0.002t$ with $t$ in months.

(a) Find $P'(y)$, naming the rule you use.

(b) Find $P(0.04)$ and $P'(0.04)$, to two decimal places.

(c) Use $P'(0.04)$ to estimate the price change if the yield rises by 0.001. Compare it with the exact change, and say why the estimate overshoots.

(d) Use the chain rule to find how fast the price is changing today, in £ per month.

(e) Show that $\dfrac{d}{dy}\ln P(y) = -5$. Explain in two sentences what this number tells a trader.
items.model:
**(a)** The outside is $100e^u$ and the inside is $u = -5y$, so by the chain rule $P'(y) = 100e^{-5y} \times (-5) = -500e^{-5y}$.

**(b)** $P(0.04) = 100e^{-0.2} = 81.87$ pounds. $P'(0.04) = -500e^{-0.2} = -409.37$ pounds per unit of yield.

**(c)** The estimate is $P'(0.04) \times 0.001 = -0.4094$, a fall of about £0.41. The exact change is $100e^{-0.205} - 100e^{-0.2} = 81.4647 - 81.8731 = -0.4083$. The price curve bends upwards (it is convex), so it lies above its tangent and the tangent overstates the fall slightly.

**(d)** $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = P'(y)\,\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -409.37 \times 0.002 = -0.8187$, so the price is falling about £0.82 a month.

**(e)** $\ln P = \ln 100 - 5y$, so $\dfrac{d}{dy}\ln P = -5$. Equivalently $\dfrac{P'}{P} = \dfrac{-500e^{-5y}}{100e^{-5y}} = -5$. The price falls about 5% for every 0.01 rise in the yield, whatever the yield is. That number is the bond's duration, 5 years, the standard measure of its interest-rate risk.

rubric.text: Finds $P'(y) = -500e^{-5y}$ and names the chain rule, with the inside derivative $-5$
Estimates −£0.41, computes the exact −£0.408, and explains the overshoot by the curve bending upwards (convexity)
Multiplies $P'(y)$ by $\tfrac{dy}{dt} = 0.002$ to get about −£0.82 a month
Shows $\tfrac{d}{dy}\ln P = -5$ and reads it as about a 5% fall per 0.01 rise in yield, the duration
